intro: In Uşak province, on a promontory ringed on three sides by deep gorges, stands Blaundus. Its story begins in the 3rd century BC, and its walls, temple and rock tombs are still largely standing. Here, the landscape itself was the first line of defence.
history: The city was built on a promontory ringed on three sides by deep gorges, a position that made it defend itself. It was founded in the Hellenistic period, grew under Rome and became a bishopric under Byzantium.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the wall and gate, the temple, the theatre and the rock tombs.
facts: Did you know? The name comes from the Macedonian soldiers settled here: inscriptions call it 'Blaundos of the Macedonians'. And the city sits on a promontory ringed on three sides by gorges, a position that defends itself.
outro: This brings our journey through Blaundus to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
